hold_text: Tier-2: the diff is in src/prop/ and it changes WHEN the operator receives a ping. It must not self-land. The operator asked for this (verbatim 2026-09-09: "This ping in the prop channel is unessacry, the account snapshot is updated when a trade closes, if there are no prop trades than the account state didn't change"), and an ask to change the TRIGGER is not an OK to ship it unread — so this declares hold and does NOT arm auto-merge or claim the merge slot. WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD ACTUALLY CHECK, because it is one decision and not the diff size: THIS CHANGE MAKES THE BOT GO QUIET ABOUT A STALE PROP BALANCE WHILE THE BOOK IS FLAT. That is safe only if a stale snapshot cannot hide a shrinking cushion, and the argument is: (a) prop_reconcile.reconstruct_equity is ASYMMETRIC by design — an unplaceable LOSS is always applied, an unplaceable GAIN is withheld and counted — so a REPORTED fill can only ever make the cushion conservative, never optimistic; (b) an OPEN position still asks, because its unrealized drawdown is invisible to the cushion and is the one genuinely unsafe case; (c) a REAL (non-suppressed) ticket taken against the cushion still asks, which is the 2026-08-14 static-DD purpose preserved and now OBSERVED rather than assumed; (d) a read we could not make asks, never suppresses. If you disagree with (a) — that is the load-bearing claim — this should not land. ⚠️ TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, both of which look like the fix: the pre-2026-08-14 `if not positions: return []` flat bail is NOT restored (it was Tier-2 operator-approved for the static-DD floor, which binds while flat), and PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS is NOT raised (four consumers share it — this ask, the fill-ack nudge, prop_balance.max_age_hours()'s SIZING gate, and /api/bot/prop/status's freshness verdict; one definition of 'too old to trust' is deliberate). ⚠️ AND ONE RESIDUAL, STATED NOT HIDDEN: going quiet while flat is only safe because SIZING hard-refuses on a stale balance, and that refusal reaches NOBODY — coordinator.py's sizing branch calls log_rejection_to_journal + logger and the operator-facing _emit_execution_failure_ping is on the later execute_pkg branch, never reached. Filed as BL-20260909-PROP-SIZING-REFUSAL-ON-A-STALE-BALANCE-IS-JOURNALED-BUT-NEVER-PINGED and deliberately not fixed here (one PR, one concern); it is why trigger (c) exists rather than trusting the gate alone.
why: MI-214, WO-20260909-PROP-STATUS-REQUEST-FIRES-ON-WALL-CLOCK-AGE-ALONE. src/prop/prop_status_request.py asked for a fresh balance on the WALL-CLOCK AGE of the last snapshot and nothing else, so an account nothing had touched was indistinguishable from one that moved and was never reported — the desensitized-alarm P1. The trigger now keys on whether anything has HAPPENED since the snapshot, via a pure `assess_activity` so the policy is arguable in tests rather than against a live prop account, with five never-collapsed states (no_snapshot / position_open / ticket_since_snapshot / quiescent / unknown). QUIESCENT is the only verdict that suppresses; UNKNOWN asks, because a read failure must never silence a safety prompt — which matters concretely, since prop_monitor_pulse.find_open_prop_positions swallows its own list_fills failure into `[]`. MEASUREMENT OF THE OPERATOR'S PREMISE, because it was a claim and it is HALF FALSE: read 2026-09-09T09:54Z from /api/bot/prop/fills?limit=500 and /api/bot/prop/status direct over the Caddy host, breakout_1's newest snapshot is id 19 at 2026-08-30T19:33:29Z and its newest fill is id 41 at 2026-08-30T19:39:00Z — the last close is 5.5 MINUTES NEWER than the snapshot it supposedly produced, so 'a close updates the snapshot' is false AS A MECHANISM; a close only PROMPTS one. The operator's conclusion holds anyway, for a stronger reason: zero fills in the 230h since, zero open positions, zero unacted tickets, and the one fill that does postdate the snapshot is a +35.28 WITHHELD GAIN (the panel shows an $87.34 cushion to the $4,700 floor where the true one is ~$122.62 — conservative, not optimistic). Separately measured for the residual above, stating the population: /api/diag/journal?table=order_packages&limit=1000 (the endpoint max) spanning 2026-08-05T03:14:04Z -> 2026-09-09T09:48:28Z, 77 rows mentioning breakout, 4 carrying prop_balance/sizing_failed — all on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-13, none since the snapshot. Those 4 are the POSITIVE CONTROL, so 'none since' is a real zero and not a broken probe; the 1000-row cap is the limit of that measurement and it is NOT a lifetime count. TESTS: 14 added (27 total in the file, all passing), and they are MUTATION-CHECKED rather than merely green — neutering the QUIESCENT gate fails 1, treating `suppressed` as exposure fails 2, collapsing UNKNOWN into QUIESCENT fails 3. ⚠️ tests/test_prop_rule_distance_freshness.py has 2 failures in this container; they REPRODUCE on a clean worktree of origin/main and are not from this diff.
